Pressed with questions he disliked, the Prophet angrily invited any question and told men who their fathers were, until Umar knelt saying they accepted Allah, Islam and Muhammad and repented.
After Zuhr the Prophet spoke of the Hour and invited questions, naming Abdullah bin Hudhafa's father, until Umar knelt declaring contentment; he said Paradise and Hell had been shown him.
After a man asked who his father was and others questioned the Prophet mockingly, the verse came forbidding questions about things which, if made plain, would cause trouble.
Angered by many questions, the Prophet offered to answer any; a man learned his father was Hudhaifa, Umar sought refuge from afflictions, and Paradise and Hell were shown to him.
Pressed with questions, the Prophet offered from the pulpit to answer any, named one man's father, and Umar sought refuge with Allah from the evil of afflictions.

Earlier nations were ruined by questions and differences over their prophets; the Prophet disliked needless questions, feared night prayer becoming obligatory and grew angry when pressed; overburdening oneself is forbidden.
